Hi Jordan,

Thanks for sending the initial SIG. Our security team had a few follow-ups specific to how Redwood describes its hosting modes. The SIG spreadsheet asks for "where processing occurs" and "who has access to keys/logs/PII" for each mode. For procurement we need a concise statement of differences between: Hosted (Redwood managed), Dedicated (customer-dedicated pools), and Private (VPC / on-prem).

Can you provide a short, plain-English mapping plus pointers to evidence artifacts (network diagrams, SOC2 sections, KMS ownership, data flows)? If you can attach a single combined PDF and a short CSV mapping, that would be ideal.

Hi Chris — thanks for the clear ask. We can do a one-page summary + an evidence bundle. Attaching a first-pass PDF and a hosting-mode matrix (see attachments).

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Hosted (Redwood API): Processing in Redwood-managed multi-tenant clusters. Customers authenticate via API keys; Redwood manages keys and KV caches; logs are retained per our SOC2 and retention policy. We provide tenant-level logical separation and TLS in transit; for keys we typically manage envelope keys unless customer requests bring-your-own-key for Dedicated/Private.
- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): Customer gets isolated GPU pools in Redwood infra. Processing occurs on customer-dedicated instances provisioned in our cloud accounts. Customers may opt for customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest keys; control plane remains Redwood-managed. Audit logs are delivered to customer destinations on request.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Deployment within customer VPC or on-premises; customer controls the network and KMS; Redwood provides a private control plane optionally via a management link. Data residency and access boundaries are controlled by the customer.

See the attached redwood-sig-evidence-20271121.pdf for more detail and the hosting matrix spreadsheet which maps SIG questions to artifacts.

I looped in Monica (security/ops) and Vivek (deploy/runtime) for technical and evidence details. If you want, we can hop on a 30-minute call Monday morning to walk the team through the matrix before you finalize the SIG.

Best,
Jordan

Hi Chris — quick technical addendum to Jordan's summary that maps directly to SIG items (short bullets):

1) Processing location / tenancy:
- Hosted: Multi-tenant compute, per-tenant logical isolation. Models run on shared clusters; we isolate request/response data in software.
- Dedicated: Single-tenant GPU pools (customer tag + isolated VMs/containers). No cross-tenant compute scheduling.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Customer-managed compute inside their network; control of network ACLs and subnets.

2) Key management:
- Hosted: Redwood-managed envelope keys (Root KMS in Redwood). Customer data keys rotated by Redwood.
- Dedicated: Option for customer-managed KMS (customer holds root) or Redwood-managed per contract.
- Private: Customer KMS only (BYOK) — Redwood does not hold root keys.

3) Logs / audit trails:
- Hosted: Centralized logs; tenant identifiers provided. We can forward S3 log bundles or provide API access to logs on request per contract.
- Dedicated: Logs collected per dedicated cluster; delivery to customer S3 or SIEM configured during provisioning.
- Private: Logs remain inside customer network; we can ship agents if requested.

4) Evidence pointers (packaged in the PDF / Drive folder):
- Network diagram: redwood-network-diagram-20271121.png
- SOC 2 sections: SOC2-report.pdf (redacted) — see SOC2 sections 3.1, 4.2 for encryption and access control
- Deployment matrix: sig-hosting-matrix.xlsx (maps SIG question IDs to artifacts and responsible owners)

If you need a line-by-line mapping of the SIG (column: question_id, answer, artifact), we can generate an exported CSV by Monday morning.

Regards,
Vivek
